newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees changes to new rice import scheme.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees changes to new rice import scheme.

text.p: The European Union agreed changes to a new cumulative recovery system for husked rice which enters into force on July 1, EU member state officials said on Friday.
"They are mostly technical changes," said an official, adding that the aim was to ensure that the new rules were fairly applied.
The amendments include a 50 Ecus a tonne penalty for any importer refusing spot checks on shipments. Previously the importer would only have been excluded from the scheme.

The optional system was agreed in April following a U.S. complaint to the World Trade Organisation concerning duty-free quotas for 8,000 tonens of brown rice and 36,000 tonnes of partly processed rice.
The system allows traders to reclaim excess import duties paid under the EU's representative price system if they can prove these are higher than levels set under the GATT Uruguay Round Agreement.
